title: Investment Committee Memos
answer: Investment committee memos are the formal documents that lay out a proposed investment, the supporting evidence, the risks, and a recommendation for a committee to decide on. In agent workflows, the scope covers how AI agents help assemble, draft, check, and route these memos, from pulling market data and filings to formatting the final packet. It includes the handoffs between research, compliance, and the committee itself, but it does not cover the committee's deliberation or the investment decision. The work is document-centric and evidence-heavy, so the agent's job is to reduce manual gathering and drafting while keeping a clear chain of sources.

sections.body: Investment committee memos are the formal documents that lay out a proposed investment, the supporting evidence, the risks, and a recommendation for a committee to decide on. In agent workflows, the scope covers how AI agents help assemble, draft, check, and route these memos, from pulling market data and filings to formatting the final packet. It includes the handoffs between research, compliance, and the committee itself, but it does not cover the committee's deliberation or the investment decision. The work is document-centric and evidence-heavy, so the agent's job is to reduce manual gathering and drafting while keeping a clear chain of sources.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The workflow runs on a stack that combines document stores, market and filing data feeds, and a large language model or a set of models accessed through an API. It typically uses retrieval augmented generation to ground each memo in approved sources, plus orchestration software to manage steps, permissions, and retries. Where the site's data is used, a memo may reference one of the 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices. The infrastructure must support access controls, versioning, and audit logs so that every figure and sentence can be traced back to its source.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The agent workflow starts with a request, often a deal or a position, and then retrieves the relevant research, financials, and prior memos. Agents extract key figures, draft sections such as the thesis, risks, and comparables, and check the draft against a compliance checklist and a house style guide. A human analyst or portfolio manager reviews the draft, corrects errors, and signs off before the memo goes to the committee. The agents may also compare the new memo to past ones to flag inconsistencies or missing sections, but they do not vote or decide.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance is central: every memo should record which sources, model versions, prompts, and edits produced each part, so the committee can see how a conclusion was reached. Rights and risk issues include data licensing, confidentiality, the handling of material nonpublic information, and the danger of hallucinated figures or stale data. A risk section may draw on the site's 148 active AI lawsuits and 215 compliance and regulation pages to show the regulatory and litigation context. Access controls, retention rules, and audit trails are part of the workflow, not an afterthought, because a memo can become a formal record.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward tighter integration with portfolio and order management systems, so that a memo's data and assumptions update automatically as markets move. Agent workflows are likely to become more transparent, with step-by-step reasoning logs and standard ways to cite sources, which helps with audit and review. We may see more multi-agent setups where one agent drafts, another challenges, and a third checks compliance, all under human supervision. The aim is to give the committee a faster, better-sourced packet while keeping human judgment and accountability in place.
